module.purpose: Implements Trailbase collection synchronization layer for TanStack DB, providing bidirectional sync between local store and Trailbase remote database with automatic ID tracking and event subscription.
module.summary: This file exports the `trailBaseCollectionOptions` function that configures a TanStack DB collection to sync with a Trailbase remote database. It handles serialization/deserialization of records, bidirectional synchronization (eager and lazy modes), real-time event subscription, and ensures transaction IDs are properly awaited for consistency. The module provides conversion utilities between internal item format and Trailbase record format, manages cursor-based pagination, and implements cleanup of expired seen IDs.
module.businessContext: Enables offline-first applications to sync data with Trailbase backend, ensuring data consistency across clients. Critical for collaborative apps where multiple users modify shared records. Failure results in data loss or inconsistency between clients.

detail.name: convert
detail.signature:
function convert<
  InputType extends ShapeOf<OutputType> & Record<string, unknown>,
  OutputType extends ShapeOf<InputType>,
>(
  conversions: Conversions<InputType, OutputType>,
  input: InputType,
): OutputType
postconditions: The returned object contains every key present in input
For each key k in input, if conversions[k] exists the returned value is conversions[k](input[k]); otherwise the returned value is input[k]
invariants: The function is pure — input and conversions are not mutated
The returned object is a new object (not reference-equal to input)
edgeCases: Empty input object produces an empty output object
All keys present in conversions produces a fully-converted output
Partial conversions map: keys absent from conversions pass through with their original value unchanged
detail.summary: Applies an optional per-key conversion map to an input object, returning a new object of the same shape. Keys without a matching conversion function pass through unchanged.

specTests.then: returns { a: 6, b: 7, c: 1 } — b passes through unchanged, a and c are transformed
returns { x: 'hello', y: 42 } — all values pass through unchanged

detail.returnType: CollectionConfig<TItem, TKey, never, TrailBaseCollectionUtils> & { utils: TrailBaseCollectionUtils }
genericTypeParams: TKey extends string | number = string | number
preconditions: config.recordApi must implement a list method accepting { pagination, order, filters } and returning { records, cursor }
config.parse must be a converter from TRecord to TItem
config.serialize must be a converter from TItem/TPartial<TItem> to TRecord
config.getKey must extract a string|number key from a TItem
postconditions: Returns a CollectionConfig object whose sync function can paginate through TrailBase records in batches of up to 256
Returns a CollectionConfig with a utils object (TrailBaseCollectionUtils) attached
Internal sync mode defaults to 'eager' when config.syncMode is not provided
invariants: seenIds Store tracks every record ID that has been written via sync, mapping string IDs to a numeric value
Cursors from prior fetches are cached per lastKey so incremental loading reuses encrypted cursor tokens
edgeCases: awaitIds called with IDs already present in seenIds resolves immediately without subscribing
awaitIds called with IDs not yet seen waits until all appear or timeout elapses, then throws TimeoutWaitingForIdsError
load with limit <= 0 returns immediately without making any API call
load when recordApi.list returns empty records array breaks the pagination loop (drained)
load when response records length < batch limit indicates end of data, causing the loop to break
cancelEventReader called when no eventReader exists is a no-op
stateMutations: seenIds Store is mutated on each sync write (insert entries)
eventReader reference is set/cleared by cancelEventReader
detail.ioFormatSpec: The sync load function calls config.recordApi.list with { pagination: { limit, offset?, cursor? }, order?, filters? } and expects back { records: TRecord[], cursor?: string }. Records are converted via config.parse before being written as { type: 'insert', value: TItem } operations.
